In mathematics, '''''k''-Hessian equations''' (or '''Hessian equations''' for short)  are [[partial differential equation]]s (PDEs) based on the [[Hessian matrix]]. More specifically, a Hessian equation is the ''k''-trace, or the ''k''th [[elementary symmetric polynomial]] of eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix. When ''k'' ≥ 2, the ''k''-Hessian equation is a fully nonlinear partial differential equation.<ref>{{citation | first1 = Andrea | last1 = Colesanti | title = On entire solutions of the Hessian equations ''S''<sub>''k''</sub>(''D''<sup>2</sup>''u'') = 1 | journal = Quaderno del Dipartimento di Matematica "U. Dini", Universitá degli Studi di Firenze | year = 2004 | url = http://web.math.unifi.it/users/colesant/ricerca/slzint.pdf }}.</ref> It can be written as <math>{\cal S}_k[u]=f</math>, where <math>1\leqslant k \leqslant n</math>, <math>{\cal S}_k[u]=\sigma_k(\lambda({\cal D}^2u))</math>, and <math>\lambda({\cal D}^2u)=(\lambda_1,\cdots,\lambda_n)</math>, are the eigenvalues of the ''Hessian matrix'' <math>{\cal D}^2u=[\partial_i \partial_ju]_{1\leq i,j \leq n}</math> and  <math>\sigma_k(\lambda)=\sum_{i_1<\cdots<i_k}\lambda_{i_1}\cdots\lambda_{i_k}</math>, is a <math>k</math> th elementary symmetric polynomial.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yourdkhany|first1=Mahdieh|last2=Nadjafikhah|first2=Mehdi|last3=Toomanian|first3=Megerdich|date=2021-08-01|title=Preliminary Group Classification and Some Exact Solutions of the 2-Hessian Equation|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s41980-020-00424-3|journal=Bulletin of the Iranian Mathematical Society|language=en|volume=47|issue=4|pages=977–994|doi=10.1007/s41980-020-00424-3|issn=1735-8515|arxiv=1902.02702|s2cid=225550133}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Froese|first1=Brittany D.|last2=Oberman|first2=Adam M.|last3=Salvador|first3=Tiago|date=2016-05-14|title=Numerical methods for the 2-Hessian elliptic partial differential equation|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/imanum/drw007|journal=IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis|volume=37|issue=1|pages=209–236|doi=10.1093/imanum/drw007|issn=0272-4979|arxiv=1502.04969}}</ref> 

Much like differential equations often study the actions of [[differential operator]]s (e.g. [[elliptic operator]]s and [[elliptic partial differential equation|elliptic equations]]), Hessian equations can be understood as simply eigenvalue equations  acted upon by the Hessian differential operator. Special cases include the [[Monge–Ampère equation]]<ref>{{citation | last1 = Wang | first1 = Xu-Jia | chapter = The ''k''-Hessian Equation | chapter-url = http://maths-people.anu.edu.au/~wang/publications/k-Hessian.pdf | editor1-first = Sun-Yung Alice | editor1-last = Chang | editor2-first = Antonio | editor2-last = Ambrosetti | editor3-first = Andrea | editor3-last = Malchiodi | title = Geometric Analysis and PDEs | series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics | volume = 1977 | year = 2009 | publisher = Springer-Verlag | isbn = 978-3-642-01673-8 }}.</ref> and [[Poisson's equation]] (the Laplacian being the trace of the Hessian matrix).  The ''2−''hessian operator also appears in conformal mapping problems.  In fact,  the ''2−''hessian equation is unfamiliar outside Riemannian geometry and elliptic regularity theory, that is closely related to the scalar curvature operator, which provides an intrinsic curvature for a three-dimensional manifold.

These equations are of interest in geometric PDEs (a subfield at the interface between both [[geometric analysis]] and PDEs) and [[differential geometry]].
